title: Ghost credits after fast-path rollback cause transient allowance surge
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Some requests that hit the new fast-path short-circuit were consuming per-key credits, then the fast-path later triggered a rollback path (dedupe/ingest-detection) which double-credited the key but never reconciled the original debit. This results in a short-lived spike in allowance for affected keys (clients can exceed intended quota briefly) and underbilling for those tokens. The issue appears when a fast-path accept followed by asynchronous dedupe causes the acknowledgement path to re-issue a credit without atomically cancelling the earlier debit.
timeline: 2025-02-11: Pager alert - spike in per-key allowed requests for multiple orgs between 17:40-17:47 UTC.
2025-02-11: Initial mitigation - throttled fast-path by reducing batch acceptance window (temporary).
2025-02-12: Reproduced locally with scripted ingest/dedupe sequence (see experiments).
2025-02-14: PoC fix implemented that forces synchronous reconcile in the fast-path acceptance flow.
2025-02-20: Observed reduced frequency but still saw race in high-concurrency repro harness.
2025-03-03: Plan to ship hotfix and longer-term atomic ledger redesign in runtime-1.23.
logs_evidence: sample log: rate-eval key=org_345 token=abcde action=ACCEPT path=fastpath request_id=rid-7f3e timestamp=2025-02-11T17:40:12Z
sample log: dedupe-detect request_id=rid-7f3e result=DUPLICATE path=async-ingest timestamp=2025-02-11T17:40:13Z
sample log: credit-apply key=org_345 amount=+1 reason=dedupe_rollforward ledger_tx=tx-983 but no corresponding rollback for tx-980
experiments: Repro harness: 200 concurrent clients hitting same route + dedupe signatures -> reproduced in ~12s median
Isolated run with quota logging enabled shows debit tx written, fast-path ack returned, async dedupe then issues compensating credit without referencing the original debit tx id
Introduced artificial 10ms delay in fast-path confirmation - reduced probability but did not eliminate race under qps>3k per-key
root_cause: Non-atomic interactions between the fast-path acceptance (optimistic short-circuit) and the async dedupe/ingest confirmation path. The ledger allowed compensating credits to be applied referencing only a request fingerprint, not the original debit transaction id, so the system never reconciled (or tombstoned) the initial debit. In high concurrency the timing window permits both debit and compensating credit to exist simultaneously for the same logical request.
proposed_short_term_fix: Make fast-path acceptance write a provisional ledger entry that is tombstoned on dedupe detection in the same atomic shard update (hotfix).
Disable the optimistic fast-path for keys with historically high concurrent dedupe rates via feature-flag rollout regionally for 24-72 hours.
Add a safety check in enforcement layer: if net delta for a key exceeds X tokens in Y seconds and there is a recent provisional entry, pause further accepts and surface an alert.
long_term_action_items: Redesign ledger transaction model to include strong referential integrity: every credit/debit must reference a canonical request_tx and reconciliation is an atomic ledger operation.
Introduce per-key sequence numbers (lightweight monotonic) to avoid out-of-order apply/compensate races across shards.
Add an idempotent replay handler for compensation ops that can detect and collapse duplicate compensating credits.
Build synthetic load tests into CI that exercise dedupe+fastpath scenarios at scale (integration harness).
risks_and_tradeoffs: Short-term provisional entries increase write amplification and slightly higher latency on the fast-path; acceptable for P0 mitigation but not ideal long-term.
Full atomic redesign will require migration and careful shard rollout to avoid large-scale reprocessing; requires cross-team coordination with storage/sharding owners.

Disabling fast-path for hotspot keys reduces throughput for those customers and may surface as increased latency; we must communicate to customers on the list and provide temporary credits if necessary.
